abstract_en: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment. The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome. Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50). Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

El tratamiento objetivo fue la hidralazina 75 mg/isosorbida dinitrato 40 mg tres veces al día (t.i.d.). La variable principal fue una combinación de hospitalización con empeoramiento de la insuficiencia cardiaca, una visita ambulatoria urgente que resultó en tratamiento intravenoso/metolazona para insuficiencia cardiaca, trasplante cardíaco, implantación del dispositivo de asistencia ventricular izquierda o muerte. Los criterios de valoración secundarios incluyeron componentes del resultado primario. En general, 592 pacientes predominantemente blancos (mediana de edad 72 años, 18% mujeres) fueron aleatorizados con un seguimiento medio de 3,7 años. El resultado primario se produjo en 90 de 294 pacientes (30,6%) en el grupo H-ISDN y en 91 de 298 pacientes (30,5%) en el grupo placebo [hazard ratio (HR) 0,90; 95% intervalo de confianza (IC) 0,67-1,21; P = 0,48]. Hubo 57 muertes en el grupo H-ISDN frente a 72 en el grupo placebo (HR 0,72; 95% IC 0,51-1,02); se produjo un empeoramiento de los eventos de insuficiencia cardiaca en 52 frente a 47 pacientes (HR 1,01; 95% IC 0,68-1,50%).

abstract_en: The primary aim was to evaluate, using aggregate-data meta-regression, whether body weight loss induced by incretin mimetic therapy is associated with reductions in three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE), individual cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. A secondary aim was to estimate the overall cardiovascular effects of incretin mimetics compared with placebo. A systematic review of placebo-controlled randomized trials was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible trials reported cardiovascular hazard ratios (HRs) and weight changes. The primary analysis was an aggregate-data meta-regression, with the prespecified moderator defined as the placebo-adjusted percentage weight difference at the latest reported follow-up time point. Standard meta-analysis was performed to estimate overall treatment effects. Sixteen randomized trials including 97 199 participants with and without diabetes were analysed. Meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between greater body weight loss and treatment HRs for 3P-MACE, cardiovascular or all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). These findings do not establish an individual-level or causal relationship. Meta-analysis showed significant reductions in 3P-MACE (15%), cardiovascular mortality (13%), all-cause mortality (12%), myocardial infarction (14%), stroke (13%) and HHF (10%). Greater trial-level placebo-adjusted body weight loss was not significantly associated with lower treatment HRs for the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes examined, including 3P-MACE and HHF. These findings do not exclude an individual-level contribution of weight loss to cardiovascular benefit or establish causality. Individual-participant-level analyses are needed to clarify the relationship between weight loss and cardiovascular outcomes.

abstract_en: On-pump (ONCAB) and off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) remain established approaches to surgical myocardial revascularization, but contemporary evidence does not support a universal preference for either technique. The clinically relevant question is which patient and operative setting are most likely to benefit from each strategy. We performed a contemporary narrative evidence synthesis of landmark randomized trials, long-term follow-up studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, observational cohorts, graft-patency studies, and major coronary revascularization guidelines. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for studies published from 2009 through 2025. Evidence was organized around perioperative neurologic, renal, bleeding, and respiratory outcomes; completeness of revascularization; graft patency; conversion to cardiopulmonary bypass; surgical experience; and long-term survival. No de novo meta-analysis was performed, and all pooled estimates reported in this review are explicitly attributed to previously published evidence syntheses. Randomized evidence indicates broadly similar long-term mortality between OPCAB and ONCAB, whereas OPCAB may reduce selected perioperative complications, particularly stroke, transfusion, acute kidney injury, and respiratory morbidity in appropriately selected patients. Conversely, complex coronary anatomy may favor ONCAB because a stable operative field can facilitate complete revascularization. Conversion from OPCAB to cardiopulmonary bypass is consistently associated with worse outcomes, underscoring the importance of surgeon and institutional experience. Graft-patency differences are most evident for saphenous vein grafts and technically challenging territories. Anaortic or no-touch OPCAB may be particularly valuable in patients with extensive ascending-aortic atherosclerosis. ONCAB and OPCAB should therefore be viewed as complementary strategies. Selection should integrate aortic pathology, ventricular function, renal and bleeding risk, coronary complexity, the probability of complete revascularization, and local OPCAB expertise. A patient-tailored framework can help translate heterogeneous comparative evidence into practical clinical decision-making.

Los abordajes de revascularización miocárdica quirúrgica (ONCAB) y de bypass coronario fuera de la bomba (OPCAB) siguen siendo establecidos, pero la evidencia contemporánea no apoya una preferencia universal por ninguna de las dos técnicas. La cuestión clínicamente relevante es cuál es el entorno paciente y operativo que más probablemente se beneficiará de cada estrategia. Realizamos una síntesis narrativa contemporánea de evidencias de ensayos aleatorios históricos, estudios de seguimiento a largo plazo, revisiones sistemáticas y metaanálisis, cohortes observacionales, estudios de patentabilidad de injertos y guías de revascularización coronaria mayores. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, la Biblioteca Cochrane y Web of Science fueron buscados por estudios publicados desde 2009 hasta 2025. La evidencia fue organizada en torno a resultados neurológicos, renales, hemorrágicos y respiratorios perioperatorios; integridad de la revascularización; patencia del injerto; conversión a bypass cardiopulmonar; experiencia quirúrgica; y supervivencia a largo plazo. No se realizó metaanálisis de novo, y todas las estimaciones agrupadas reportadas en esta revisión se atribuyen explícitamente a síntesis de evidencias publicadas previamente. La evidencia aleatoria indica una mortalidad ampliamente similar a largo plazo entre la OPCAB y la ONCAB, mientras que la OPCAB puede reducir las complicaciones perioperatorias seleccionadas, en particular el accidente cerebrovascular, la transfusión, la lesión renal aguda y la morbilidad respiratoria en pacientes adecuadamente seleccionados. Por el contrario, la anatomía coronaria compleja puede favorecer la ONCAB porque un campo operativo estable puede facilitar la revascularización completa. La conversión de la OPCAB a la derivación cardiopulmonar se asocia consistentemente con peores resultados, subrayando la importancia de la experiencia del cirujano y de la institución. La OPCAB anaórtica o sin contacto puede ser particularmente valiosa en pacientes con aterosclerosis ascendente extensa, por lo que debe considerarse como estrategias complementarias la selección debe integrar patología aórtica, función ventricular, riesgo renal y hemorrágico, complejidad coronaria, probabilidad de revascularización completa y experiencia local de la OPCAB. Un marco adaptado al paciente puede ayudar a traducir la evidencia comparativa heterogénea en la toma de decisiones clínicas prácticas.

abstract_en:
Background
Coronary artery disease frequently coexists in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), yet the benefit of routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR remains uncertain.Objectives
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of routine PCI before TAVR compared with conservative or deferred revascularization.Methods
We pooled randomized clinical trials comparing PCI before TAVR versus no/deferred PCI in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease. Random-effects models estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bayesian sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were performed.Results
Three trials included 1156 patients (PCI, n = 579; no/deferred PCI, n = 577). In comparator arms reporting postrandomization PCI/revascularization, 72 of 461 patients (15.6%) underwent subsequent PCI/revascularization. PCI did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiac events (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.70-1.18; I2 = 36.9%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.45-1.63; I2 = 49.8%), all-cause death (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.70-1.15; I2 = 0.0%), or stroke (RR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48-1.03; P = 0.069; I2 = 0.0%). In two trials, PCI reduced urgent revascularization (RR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.87; I2 = 54.5%) but increased major bleeding (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32; I2 = 37.9%) and any bleeding (RR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.47; I2 = 66.7%). Bayesian analyses were directionally concordant. Trial sequential analysis was inconclusive for all efficacy outcomes.Conclusion
Routine PCI before TAVR reduced urgent revascularization but increased bleeding, without significant differences in other outcomes. Current evidence remains underpowered to rule out benefit for other ischemic outcomes; larger trials are needed.

abstract_en: Background Oral anticoagulation (OAC) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) reduces ischaemic stroke (IS), but increases bleeding, including intracranial haemorrhage (ICH). As catheter ablation reduces AF burden and IS risk, we evaluated the net clinical benefit (NCB) of continuing versus discontinuing OAC after AF ablation. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing OAC continuation versus discontinuation after AF ablation. NCB was calculated as the reduction in IS with continued OAC minus 1.5 × the increase in ICH. Results Thirty-eight studies were included (3 RCTs, 35 cohort studies), enrolling 280,415 patients, with 2.7 years' follow-up. In RCTs, there was no difference between patients on-OAC vs. off-OAC for IS, major bleeding, ICH, or NCB. In cohort studies, IS was similar, but major bleeding (OR, 3.02; 95%CI, 2.06-4.42, p<0.001) and ICH (OR, 3.65; 95%CI, 2.31-5.77, p<0.001) increased, with net clinical harm (NCB -0.46; 95% CI, -0.82 to -0.10, p=0.012). Combining all studies, IS was similar, but major bleeding (OR, 2.93; 95% CI, 2.08-4.14, p<0.001) and ICH (OR, 3.63; 95% CI, 2.34-5.63, p<0.001) were increased with continued OAC, with NCB favouring discontinuation (NCB -0.46; 95% CI, -0.77 to -0.14, p=0.004). Conclusion The benefit of OAC thromboprophylaxis is attenuated after AF ablation but contributes to bleeding, supporting consideration of OAC discontinuation post-ablation. However, this cannot be extrapolated to the highest ischaemic risk patients and, as risks are dynamic and sinus rhythm maintenance is not guaranteed, close surveillance would be essential if considering this approach.

Antecedentes La anticoagulación oral (OAC) en pacientes con fibrilación auricular (AF) reduce el ictus isquémico (IS), pero aumenta el sangrado, incluyendo hemorragia intracraneal (ICH). A medida que la ablación del catéter reduce la carga de FA y el riesgo de IS, se evaluó el beneficio clínico neto (NCB) de continuar versus interrumpir el OAC después de la ablación de FA. Métodos Se realizó una revisión sistemática y metaanálisis de ensayos controlados aleatorizados (RCT) y estudios de cohorte comparando la continuación del OAC frente a la interrupción después de la ablación de FA. El ONC se calculó como la reducción en el IS con OAC continuado menos 1,5 × el aumento en el ICH. Resultados Se incluyeron 38 estudios (3 ECA, 35 estudios de cohortes), con 280.415 pacientes, con seguimiento de 2,7 años. En los ECA, no hubo diferencia entre pacientes con CAO-OAC-OAC-OAC-IS, hemorragia mayor, HCI o NCB. En los estudios de cohortes, la IA fue similar, pero la hemorragia mayor (OR, 3,02; IC95%, 2,06-4,42, p<0,001) y la HIC (OR, 3,65; IC95%, 2,31-5,77, p<0,001) aumentaron, con daño clínico neto (NCB -0,46; IC95%, -0,82 a -0,10, p=0,012). La combinación de todos los estudios fue similar, pero la hemorragia mayor (OR, 2,93; IC 95%, 2,08-4,14, p<0,001) e IC (OR, 3,63; IC 95%, 2,34-5,63, p<0,001) se incrementó con la continuación de la OAC, favoreciendo la interrupción de la OAC (NCB -0,46; IC 95%, -0,77 a -0,14; p=0,004). Conclusión El beneficio de la tromboprofilaxis OAC se atenúa después de la ablación de FA pero contribuye a la hemorragia, apoyando la consideración de la interrupción de la OAC después de la ablación; sin embargo, no se puede extrapolar a los pacientes de mayor riesgo isquémico y, como los riesgos son dinámicos y no se garantiza el mantenimiento del ritmo sinusal, sería esencial una estrecha vigilancia si se considera este enfoque.

abstract_en:
Background
Cardiovascular death (CVD) remains a leading cause of global mortality. Although semaglutide reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), the consistency and exact magnitude of its standalone effect on CVD across various patient phenotypes require comprehensive evaluation. This meta-analysis systematically evaluated the clinical efficacy of semaglutide on CVD risk across randomized controlled trials (RCTs).Methods
PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 to identify RCTs comparing semaglutide with placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), overweight or obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or chronic kidney disease, reporting CVD as a primary, secondary or exploratory outcome. Pooled hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model. Publication bias and study robustness were assessed via Egger's test, Begg's test, and trim-and-fill analysis.Results
Seven high-quality RCTs comprising 38412 patients were included. Semaglutide significantly reduced the risk of CVD by 17% compared with placebo (pooled HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72-0.95; P = 0.01). Inter-study heterogeneity was low-to-moderate (I 2= 27.44%, P = 0.18). abstract_en: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. Evidence from clinical trials and observational data shows that early rhythm control, especially with catheter ablation, results in a reduction in stroke risk and/or the reduction in AF burden. The question arises therefore, whether in patients with intermediate or low stroke risk after successful catheter ablation, whether or not to continue or discontinue OAC. Recent randomized trials and observational data have created some debate about whether OAC can be routinely stopped after a successful catheter ablation procedure, without a higher risk of thromboembolism. In this pro/contra article, we will debate the arguments for and against the cessation of anti-coagulation after catheter ablation, in the context of recent evidence from clinical trials, observational data, and meta-analysis.

Los pilares del manejo de la fibrilación auricular (AF) incluyen la prevención de accidentes cerebrovasculares, las decisiones centradas en los síntomas del paciente sobre el control del ritmo o la tasa, y el manejo proactivo de las comorbilidades y los cambios en el estilo de vida. Estos pilares no están aislados; son complementarios entre sí. Si bien los anticoagulantes orales (OAC) son altamente eficaces para reducir el accidente cerebrovascular y la mortalidad por cualquier causa en pacientes con FA, estos fármacos confieren un riesgo de sangrado mayor, incluyendo sangrado intracraneal. Por lo tanto, se plantea la cuestión de si en pacientes con riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular intermedio o bajo después de una ablación exitosa del catéter, continuar o no continuar o interrumpir el tratamiento con ACO. En recientes ensayos aleatorizados y datos observacionales se ha generado algún debate sobre si el ACO puede detenerse rutinariamente después de un procedimiento de ablación exitosa del catéter, sin un mayor riesgo de tromboembolismo. En este artículo pro/contra, se debatirán los argumentos a favor y en contra del cese de la anticoagulación después de la ablación del catéter, en el contexto de las evidencias recientes de ensayos clínicos, datos observacionales y metaanálisis.

abstract_en:
Aims
To evaluate the association of PCSK9-targeting therapies with mortality and cardiovascular events in stable or clinically stabilized randomized trial populations.Methods
We systematically reviewed randomized trials comparing alirocumab, evolocumab or inclisiran with placebo or active control. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261395609). Treatment effects were pooled as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) using random-effects models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were based on trial-level known atherosclerosis status, as defined by enrollment criteria.Results
Thirty-two trials enrolled 77,178 participants. Individual atherosclerosis status could not be determined beyond trial-level eligibility criteria. Mortality estimates were predominantly informed by large cardiovascular outcome trials. All-cause mortality was lower with PCSK9-targeting therapy (IRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95). Estimates favored PCSK9-targeting treatment in both trials requiring known atherosclerosis for enrollment (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.98) and trials without such an enrollment requirement (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.97; interaction p = 0.21). PCSK9-targeting treatment additionally reduced myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization rates. Leave-one-out estimates remained directionally consistent.Conclusion
PCSK9-targeting therapies were associated with lower all-cause mortality and fewer ischemic events across trial populations. The predominant contribution of large cardiovascular outcome trials enrolling populations with known atherosclerosis and using PCSK9 antibodies limits the ability to infer a survival benefit in populations not selected on the basis of atherosclerosis status and across individual therapies, particularly inclisiran.

abstract_en:
Abstract  Objectives:  Postoperative adverse events (AEs) remain a major source of morbidity and mortality following thoracic surgery. Current preoperative risk assessment tools have limited ability to predict individual postoperative complications. Cardiopulmonary variability assessment (CPVA), including heart rate variability (HRV) and respiratory rate variability (RRV), has emerged as a potential biomarker of autonomic function and physiologic reserve. This systematic review evaluated the role of preoperative CPVA in predicting postoperative AEs following thoracic surgery. Methods:
 A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to identify studies evaluating preoperative HRV and/or RRV as predictors of postoperative AEs in adults undergoing thoracic surgery. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, case-control studies, and diagnostic accuracy studies. Study characteristics, CPVA methodology, comparator assessments, postoperative outcomes, and risk of bias were extracted and evaluated using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and QUADAS-2. Results:
 Five cohort studies comprising 693 patients met the inclusion criteria. Four studies evaluated pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer and one evaluated esophagectomy. Three studies assessed HRV directly, while two evaluated functional measures of cardiopulmonary reserve. Reduced preoperative HRV, particularly lower root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) and high-frequency power (HFP), was associated with postoperative pneumonia, atrial fibrillation, and delirium. Lower RMSSD (OR 0.812, 95% CI 0.720–0.912) and HFP (OR 0.990, 95% CI 0.983–0.996) independently predicted postoperative pneumonia, with good discrimination (AUC 0.867). Risk of bias was low to moderate. Conclusions:
 Preoperative CPVA, particularly HRV, is a promising non-invasive biomarker for predicting postoperative AEs following thoracic surgery. Reduced HRV was consistently associated with pulmonary, cardiac, and neurologic complications. Larger prospective multicentre studies using standardized acquisition and analysis protocols are required to establish the incremental value of CPVA beyond current preoperative risk assessment tools.

abstract_en:
Background
Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high-risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL-C targets. Enlicitide (MK-0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9-directed therapies.Objective
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of enlicitide in adults with hypercholesterolemia and assess its dose-dependent effects on lipid parameters.Methods
We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through March 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation was performed. The primary outcome was the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline. Secondary outcomes included non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), lipoprotein(a), triglycerides, and safety outcomes. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2.0 and GRADE.Results
Three placebo-controlled RCTs involving 3593 participants were included. Enlicitide significantly reduced LDL-C compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], -56.19%; 95% CI, -64.14 to -48.25; p 2 = 56.9%). Significant reductions were also observed in non-HDL-C (MD, -51.36%), ApoB (MD, -47.09%), lipoprotein(a) (MD, -20.10%), and triglycerides (MD, -13.12%). A numerical dose-response gradient was observed, although subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and treatment discontinuation were comparable between groups.Conclusion
Enlicitide produced substantial reductions in LDL-C and other atherogenic lipid parameters without an apparent increase in adverse events. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials, moderate heterogeneity, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Dose-response, duration-related lipoprotein(a), and triglyceride findings were exploratory and substantially driven by single trials. Long-term cardiovascular outcomes trials are needed to establish clinical benefit.

Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. abstract_en:
Background
Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and many high-risk patients fail to reach LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) targets on statins alone. Evolocumab, a PCSK9 inhibitor, offers potent LDL-C lowering, but a synthesis of its lipid and clinical benefits in secondary prevention is needed.Methods
We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials evaluating evolocumab in adults with established cardiovascular disease. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2025. Outcomes included lipid parameters, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), individual cardiovascular endpoints, and safety, with pooled risk ratios (RR) and mean differences calculated using random-effects models.Results
Nine trials enrolling 67,662 patients were included. Evolocumab significantly reduced LDL-C (mean difference -57.73 mg/dL), total cholesterol (-52.27 mg/dL), triglycerides (-21.21 mg/dL), and lipoprotein(a) (-10.99 mg/dL), while increasing HDL-cholesterol (3.69 mg/dL). Evolocumab was associated with lower MACE (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.40-0.71), though this estimate should be interpreted cautiously given heterogeneity in endpoint definitions and study designs. Myocardial infarction (RR 0.74) and coronary revascularisation (RR 0.80) were significantly reduced, while cardiovascular mortality and stroke showed no statistically definitive reduction. Serious adverse events and neurocognitive effects were comparable between groups, though injection-site reactions were more frequent with evolocumab.Conclusion
In patients with established cardiovascular disease, evolocumab provides substantial lipid lowering and reduces ischemic events without major safety concerns, supporting its use as an adjunct to statin therapy in secondary prevention.

Background
Optimal glucose targets for critically ill patients are likely to vary by underlying condition, yet a 'one-size-fits-all' approach persists.Aim
Determining disease-specific glucose thresholds may help achieve the lowest mortality rates.Study design
This study combined a retrospective cohort analysis of the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV (MIMIC-IV) database with a frequentist network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The glucose control targets, measured by time-weighted average glucose (TWAg), were categorized into four strata: strict, intermediate strict, liberal and very liberal control.Results

This study provides evidence that optimal glucose targets in the ICU are disease-specific. In the retrospective analysis, intermediate strict control was associated with the lowest mortality in sepsis and cardiac disease, while strict control may benefit neurological patients without excess hypoglycaemia. However, for cardiac disease, the NMA ranked liberal control highest, leaving the optimal target uncertain.Relevance to clinical practice
These findings may support a pathophysiology-guided, individualized approach to glycaemic management in critically ill patients.

abstract_en:
Background
Esophageal thermal injury remains a clinically significant complication of radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), with endoscopically detected esophageal lesions (EDELs) occurring in up to 10-15% of cases and atrio-esophageal fistula carrying high mortality. Multiple protective strategies have been proposed; however, their comparative efficacy remains uncertain.Methods
We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating esophageal protection strategies during AF ablation. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through August 7, 2026. Parallel-group randomized trials in adult patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation were included. The primary outcome was incidence of EDEL. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed, with treatment hierarchy assessed using P-scores. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2 and CINeMA frameworks, respectively.Results
Twenty-five randomized controlled trials involving approximately 2,500 patients were included in the systematic review. Twelve trials involving 1,077 patients contributed to the connected network meta-analysis. Mechanical esophageal deviation combined with luminal esophageal temperature monitoring (LET) had the most favorable point estimate compared with no dedicated protection (OR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.02-3.05) and achieved the highest P-score (0.861). The rankogram estimated a 58% probability of ranking first. Visualization-guided strategies also showed a favorable point estimate (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.08-3.09), whereas LET alone and active cooling did not demonstrate significant reductions in EDEL. Directly, mechanical deviation plus LET significantly reduced the odds of EDEL compared with single-sensor LET (OR, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.04-0.41). Seven randomized trials involving 990 patients showed no significant association between higher- versus standard-power ablation and EDEL (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.56-2.54), with no observed heterogeneity (I² = 0%). Network heterogeneity was moderate (I² = 46.9%), with no significant evidence of network inconsistency or publication bias.Conclusions
No single esophageal protection strategy completely eliminates the risk of thermal injury during AF ablation. Mechanical esophageal deviation combined with LET demonstrated the most favorable overall ranking, while visualization-guided strategies also showed a potentially beneficial signal. In contrast, LET or cooling alone did not reliably reduce EDEL incidence. However, overall confidence in the evidence is constrained by small trial samples and reliance on surrogate outcomes. Larger, contemporary trials are needed to confirm clinical benefits and assess the impact on rare but catastrophic complications.Clinical trial number

Se incluyeron ensayos aleatorizados de grupos paralelos en pacientes adultos sometidos a ablación por radiofrecuencia, siendo el resultado primario la incidencia de EDEL, se realizó un metaanálisis de la red de efectos aleatorios frecuente, se evaluó la jerarquía del tratamiento mediante puntuaciones P, se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo y la certeza de la evidencia utilizando los marcos Cochrane RoB 2 y CINeMA, respectivamente.Resultados Veinticinco ensayos aleatorizados controlados en los que participaron aproximadamente 2.500 pacientes en la revisión sistemática, y 12 ensayos en los que participaron 1.077 pacientes contribuyeron al metaanálisis de la red conectada. La desviación esofágica mecánica combinada con la monitorización luminal de la temperatura esofágica (LET) tuvo la estimación de punto más favorable en comparación con la no protección dedicada (OR, 0,27; IC 95%, 0,02-3,05) y alcanzó la puntuación P más alta (0,861). El ranking estimó una probabilidad de clasificación del 58%. Las estrategias guiadas por visualización también mostraron una estimación de punto favorable (OR, 0,48; IC 95%, 0,08-3,09), mientras que LET solo y el enfriamiento activo no mostraron reducciones significativas en EDEL. Directamente, la desviación mecánica más LET redujo significativamente las probabilidades de EDEL en comparación con el LET de un solo sensor (OR, 0,13; IC 95%, 0,04-0,41). Siete ensayos aleatorizados en los que participaron 990 pacientes no mostraron asociación significativa entre la ablación de potencia superior versus estándar y la EDEL (OR, 1,19; IC 95%, 0,56-2,54), sin heterogeneidad observada (I2 = 0%).La heterogeneidad de la red fue moderada (I2 = 46,9%), sin evidencia significativa de inconsistencia de la red o sesgo de publicación.Conclusiones Ninguna estrategia de protección esofágica única elimina por completo el riesgo de lesión térmica durante la ablación de FA.La desviación esofágica mecánica combinada con LET demostró la clasificación global más favorable, mientras que las estrategias guiadas por visualización también mostraron una señal potencialmente beneficiosa. Por el contrario, LET o enfriamiento por sí solos no redujeron de manera fiable la incidencia de EDEL. Sin embargo, la confianza general en la evidencia se ve limitada por pequeñas muestras de ensayo y la dependencia de los resultados sustitutos.Se necesitan ensayos más grandes y contemporáneos para confirmar los beneficios clínicos y evaluar el impacto en complicaciones raras pero catastróficas.

abstract_en:
Background
Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors have become a key drug class in the treatment of Type 2 diabetes (T2D) due to their effectiveness in blood sugar control, but also for many other clinical indications because of beneficial effects on cardiovascular diseases and mortality. Therefore, the findings of a secondary analysis of the recent EMMY trial, in which acute myocardial infarction patients treated with empagliflozin had higher trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) serum levels compared to placebo, were unexpected, as high TMAO concentrations in blood have previously been linked to adverse cardiovascular and mortality outcomes. In light of this, the aim of our study was to explore the effects of the SGLT-2 inhibitors empagliflozin and dapagliflozin on plasma concentrations and renal clearance (ClR) in a T2D patient setting.Methods
Plasma and 24-h urine samples from two prospective, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, cross-over trials with T2D patients (empagliflozin N = 69, NCT02471963; dapagliflozin N = 54, NCT02383238), taken at baseline and after each treatment with either SGLT-2 inhibitor or placebo, were measured for TMAO via LC-MS/MS.Results
After treatment with an SGLT-2 inhibitor, in the total of 123 patients, TMAO plasma levels were 11.5% higher compared to placebo (p = 0.006) and ClR of TMAO was reduced by 10.3% (p = 0.048) without any relevant change in its urinary excretion (p = 0.521). In the dapagliflozin trial, TMAO plasma concentration was 23.4% higher (p = 0.021), and ClR of TMAO was 22.6% lower (p = 0.025) after treatment with dapagliflozin compared to placebo. For empagliflozin, a similar trend was observed, but did not reach statistical significance.Conclusion
Treatment with an SGLT-2 inhibitor was associated with a modest increase in plasma concentration of TMAO. Together with data from a previous trial, the present findings suggest a possible class effect of SGLT-2 inhibitors. Whether this effect impacts the overall clinical benefits of SGLT-2 inhibitors needs to be subject to further investigations.Trial registration

title: The Effect of Perioperative Video Interventions on Postoperative Pain Control: A Systematic Review.
short: The Effect of Perioperative Video Interventions on Postoperative Pain Control: A Systematic Review.

abstract_en:
Introduction
Postoperative pain is a major cause of suffering and is linked to serious complications, including delayed wound healing, increased cardiovascular risk, delayed rehabilitation, and chronic postsurgical pain. Modifiable psychological factors influence pain outcomes, and preliminary evidence suggests video interventions can reduce preoperative anxiety and improve patient satisfaction. We hypothesized that video interventions could improve postoperative pain control. Therefore, the aim of the current systematic review was to summarize all previous research and investigate the effects of perioperative video interventions on pain levels and/or analgesic consumption.Methods
The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024596389) and followed the PRISMA Guidelines. We searched PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Academic Search, and the Cochrane Central register of controlled trials from inception to October 2025 for randomized controlled trials in adult surgical patients. Trials assessing any perioperative video interventions reporting on postoperative pain intensity and/or analgesic consumption were included. Data was extracted independently by two authors, and data synthesis was qualitative due to significant heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).Results
Forty-four trials were included. Of the 42 trials assessing pain, 11 (26%) reported significantly lower pain in the intervention group. Of the 19 trials measuring analgesic consumption, eight (42%) reported significantly lower consumption in the intervention group. Only two trials demonstrated a benefit for both co-primary outcomes. Significant improvements in secondary outcomes, including anxiety, physical function, and satisfaction, were reported in 26 trials. Most trials were judged as having a high risk of bias.Conclusion
The current systematic review suggests that perioperative video interventions may improve acute postoperative pain control, although effects are inconsistent across trials. Future research should focus on identifying patient and intervention characteristics that predict efficacy to guide clinical implementation.Editorial comment
This trustworthy systematic review presents an overview of current research findings for application of perioperative video-based treatments as part of managing postoperative pain. While this approach shows promise, more definitive evidence may be needed to justify more widespread implementation.

title: Bexagliflozin: pharmacological profile and clinical applications of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
short: Bexagliflozin: pharmacological profile and clinical applications of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.

abstract_en: Bexagliflozin, approved in the United States in 2023, is the fifth selective sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Unlike other class members, it lacks an event-driven cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) and trials with hard kidney or heart failure endpoints. This narrative mini-review separates bexagliflozin-specific evidence from class benefits. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles (January 2009-June 2026) using "bexagliflozin," "Brenzavvy," and "SGLT2 inhibitor," plus prescribing information and pivotal class trials. Randomized trials and meta-analyses were prioritized. Bexagliflozin reduced glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), body weight, and systolic blood pressure vs. placebo and was noninferior to sitagliptin, glimepiride, and, in one 24-week trial, dapagliflozin for HbA1c. In stage 3a/3b chronic kidney disease, it reduced albuminuria by 20.1 % vs. placebo, a surrogate finding. A cardiovascular safety trial and meta-analysis excluded excess cardiovascular risk but were not powered for benefit. Adverse events were consistent with the class. Bexagliflozin is an effective glucose-lowering drug, but its cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure benefits remain unproven and cannot be assumed from class data. Outcome-proven agents are preferred for cardiorenal protection. An adequately powered CVOT and hard kidney endpoint trials are the key research priorities.

Bexagliflozina, aprobada en los Estados Unidos en 2023, es el quinto inhibidor selectivo de la cotransportadora de glucosa de sodio 2 (SGLT2) para la diabetes mellitus tipo 2 (T2DM). A diferencia de otros miembros de la clase, carece de un ensayo de resultados cardiovasculares impulsados por eventos (CVOT) y de ensayos con variables de insuficiencia renal o cardíaca. Esta mini-revisión narrativa separa la evidencia específica de bexagliflozina de los beneficios de clase. PubMed y Google Scholar fueron buscados por artículos en inglés (enero de 2009-junio de 2026) usando "bexagliflozina", "Brenzavvy" e "Inhibidor de la SGLT2", además de prescribir información y ensayos de clase pivotal. La bexagliflozina redujo la hemoglobina glicada (HbA1c), el peso corporal y la presión arterial sistólica frente a placebo y no fue inferior a la sitagliptina, la glimepirida y, en un ensayo de 24 semanas, la dapagliflozina para la HbA1c. En el estadio 3a/3b de la enfermedad renal crónica, redujo la albuminuria en un 20,1 % frente a placebo, un hallazgo sustituto. Un ensayo de seguridad cardiovascular y un metaanálisis excluyeron el exceso de riesgo cardiovascular, pero no fueron potenciados para obtener beneficios. Los eventos adversos fueron consistentes con la clase. La bexagliflozina es un fármaco eficaz que reduce la glucosa, pero sus beneficios cardiovasculares, renales y de insuficiencia cardíaca siguen sin ser probados y no se pueden asumir de los datos de clase. Para la protección cardiorrenal se prefieren agentes probados con resultados. Las principales prioridades de la investigación son un CVOT con una potencia adecuada y los ensayos de valoración renal dura.

abstract_en: Remifentanil infusion titrated to effect-site concentration (Ce) is commonly used to suppress coughing during emergence from general anesthesia; nevertheless, the optimal Ce range remains unclear. We aimed to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the existing evidence on the optimal Ce values of remifentanil for cough suppression during emergence. We performed a comprehensive literature search using PubMed®, Embase®, Web of Science™, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar on 27 February 2025. We included prospective studies that used the up-and-down method to estimate the effective concentrations of remifentanil in 50% of patients (EC50) and 95% of patients (EC95) for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia with tracheal intubation in adult patients. We excluded studies in children or patients undergoing cardiac surgery, as well as those that only compared predefined Ce targets of remifentanil to determine optimal dosing. We obtained pooled estimates using a random-effects model with inverse-variance method, and heterogeneity was quantified using the I2 statistic. We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool for randomized trials and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies for nonrandomized comparative or single-arm studies. The primary outcome was EC50 estimated using the up-and-down method, with secondary outcomes including model-based EC50 and EC95 estimates. We included 22 prospective studies comprising 857 adult participants, and none were assessed as being at a high risk of bias or of low methodologic quality. Based on 28 groups and 653 participants across 17 studies, the pooled mean EC50 from the up-and-down method was 2.0 ng·mL-1 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.8 to 2.3), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 74.5%). Based on 29 groups and 693 participants across 18 studies, the model-based EC50 was 1.9 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 1.6 to 2.1), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 96.1%). Based on 31 groups and 809 participants across 20 studies, the model-based EC95 was 2.7 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 2.5 to 3.0), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 99.5%). Subgroup analyses revealed higher mean EC50 values in male individuals (2.6 ng·mL-1) and the highest mean EC50 in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracic surgery (2.6 ng·mL-1). Using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework, the certainty of evidence was rated as very low for all outcomes. The identified EC50 and EC95 values of remifentanil for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults were 2.0 and 2.7 ng·mL-1, respectively. Patient sex and surgical type may influence the required Ce. Careful dose adjustment is recommended to avoid delayed awakening and hypoventilation, especially in cases requiring higher concentrations. La infusión de remifentanilo, valorada para la concentración en el lugar de efecto (Ce), se utiliza comúnmente para suprimir la tos durante la aparición de la anestesia general; sin embargo, el rango óptimo de ce sigue sin estar claro. Nuestro objetivo es realizar una revisión sistemática y un metaanálisis para sintetizar la evidencia existente sobre los valores óptimos de ce de remifentanilo para la supresión de la tos durante la aparición. Se incluyeron estudios prospectivos que utilizaron el método ascendente y descendente para estimar las concentraciones efectivas de remifentanilo en el 50% de los pacientes (EC50) y 95% de los pacientes (EC95) para suprimir la tos durante la emergencia de anestesia general con intubación traqueal en pacientes adultos, se excluyeron los estudios en niños o pacientes sometidos a cirugía cardiaca, así como aquellos que sólo compararon objetivos de remifentanilo C predefinidos para determinar la dosis óptima, se obtuvieron estimaciones agrupadas mediante un modelo de efectos aleatorios con método de variación inversa y se cuantificó la heterogeneidad mediante la estadística I2. Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo utilizando la herramienta Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 para ensayos aleatorizados y el Índice Metodológico para Estudios No Randomizados para estudios comparativos o monofarmacéuticos no aleatorizados, el resultado primario fue EC50 estimado utilizando el método ascendente y descendente, con resultados secundarios incluyendo modelos basados en EC50 y EC95 estimados. Se incluyeron 22 estudios prospectivos con 857 participantes adultos, y ninguno fue evaluado como de alto riesgo de sesgo o de baja calidad metodológica. Con base en 28 grupos y 653 participantes en 17 estudios, la media EC50 agrupada del método up-and-down fue de 2,0 ng·mL-1 (intervalo de confianza del 95% [IC], 1,8 a 2,3), con considerable heterogeneidad (I2 = 74,5%); con base en 29 grupos y 693 participantes en 18 estudios, la EC50 basada en el modelo fue de 1,9 ng·mL-1 (IC del 95%, 1,6 a 2,1), con considerable heterogeneidad (I2 = 96,1%); con base en 31 grupos y 809 participantes en 20 estudios, la EC95 basada en el modelo fue de 2,7 ng·mL-1 (IC del 95%, 2,5 a 3,0), con considerable heterogeneidad (I2 = 99,5%). Los análisis de subgrupos revelaron valores medios más altos de EC50 en individuos varones (2,6 ng·mL-1) y la media más alta de EC50 en pacientes sometidos a cirugía torácica asistida por video (2,6 ng·mL-1). Utilizando el marco de clasificación de recomendaciones, evaluación, desarrollo y evaluación, la certeza de la evidencia fue calificada como muy baja para todos los resultados.Los valores identificados de EC50 y EC95 de remifentanilo para la supresión de la tos durante la aparición de anestesia general en adultos fueron 2,0 y 2,7 ng·mL-1, respectivamente. Se recomienda un ajuste cuidadoso de la dosis para evitar el despertar e hipoventilación tardíos, especialmente en casos que requieran concentraciones más altas.

abstract_en: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) have evolved from glucose-lowering agents to foundational therapies for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, with substantial benefits for cardiovascular, kidney, and survival outcomes. As their indications continue to expand, a comprehensive understanding of their safety and tolerability has become increasingly important for optimizing patient care. Building on our recent state-of-the-art review of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, this review provides a contemporary synthesis of the evidence on the safety and tolerability of SGLT-2is. We critically appraise data from randomized controlled trials, cardiovascular and kidney outcome trials, pharmacovigilance databases, large observational studies, and systematic reviews and meta-analyses. The available evidence demonstrates that SGLT-2is have a favorable overall safety profile, with genital mycotic infections representing the most consistently observed adverse event. Volume depletion and euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis remain clinically important but are uncommon and are largely preventable through appropriate patient selection, patient education, and temporary treatment interruption during high-risk clinical situations. Fournier's gangrene should be regarded as a very rare but serious complication requiring prompt recognition and treatment. In contrast, randomized trials and meta-analyses generally indicate a reduced risk of acute kidney injury, while evidence concerning fracture, lower-limb amputation, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and cancer is less definitive. Although consistent class-wide increases in these latter outcomes have not been established, uncommon or agent-specific risks cannot be excluded, particularly where event numbers are small or follow-up is limited. Overall, treatment discontinuation because of adverse events is low across major cardiovascular, heart failure, and kidney outcome trials, supporting the excellent tolerability of this therapeutic class. Comparative evidence suggests only modest differences among individual SGLT-2is, although definitive conclusions remain limited by the absence of direct, large, randomized head-to-head trials. We also summarize practical strategies for adverse-event mitigation, monitoring, temporary treatment interruption, and individualized patient selection. As the clinical applications of SGLT-2is continue to broaden, ongoing pharmacovigilance, inclusive clinical trials, and comparative safety studies will be essential to further refine their benefit-risk profile and optimize their safe use across diverse patient populations.

Los inhibidores del cotransportador de sodio-glucosa-2 (SGLT-2is) han evolucionado de los agentes hipoglucemiantes a las terapias fundacionales para el manejo de la diabetes mellitus tipo 2, insuficiencia cardíaca y enfermedad renal crónica, con beneficios sustanciales para los resultados cardiovasculares, renales y de supervivencia. A medida que sus indicaciones continúan expandiéndose, una comprensión integral de su seguridad y tolerabilidad se ha vuelto cada vez más importante para optimizar la atención al paciente. Se evalúan críticamente los datos de ensayos controlados aleatorizados, ensayos de desenlace cardiovascular y renal, bases de datos de farmacovigilancia, estudios observacionales de gran envergadura y revisiones sistemáticas y metaanálisis.La evidencia disponible demuestra que SGLT-2 tiene un perfil de seguridad general favorable, con infecciones micóticas genitales que representan el evento adverso más consistentemente observado. La depleción de volumen y la cetoacidosis diabética euglicémica siguen siendo clínicamente importantes, pero son poco comunes y en gran medida evitables mediante la selección adecuada de pacientes, la educación del paciente y la interrupción temporal del tratamiento durante situaciones clínicas de alto riesgo. La gangrena de Fournier debe ser considerada como una complicación muy rara pero grave que requiere un rápido reconocimiento y tratamiento. En cambio, los ensayos aleatorizados y los metaanálisis generalmente indican un menor riesgo de lesión renal aguda, mientras que la evidencia relativa a fractura, amputación de la parte baja, hepatotoxicidad, pancreatitis y cáncer es menos definitiva. Aunque no se han establecido incrementos sistemáticos de estos últimos resultados en toda la clase, no se pueden excluir los riesgos poco frecuentes o específicos de los agentes, especialmente cuando el número de eventos es pequeño o el seguimiento es limitado. En general, la interrupción del tratamiento debido a eventos adversos es baja en los ensayos cardiovasculares, de insuficiencia cardíaca y de desenlace renal, lo que apoya la excelente tolerabilidad de esta clase terapéutica. La evidencia comparativa sugiere sólo diferencias modestas entre SGLT-2is individuales, aunque las conclusiones definitivas siguen siendo limitadas por la ausencia de ensayos directos, grandes y aleatorizados cabeza a cabeza. También se resumen estrategias prácticas para la mitigación de eventos adversos, monitoreo, interrupción temporal del tratamiento y selección individualizada de pacientes. A medida que las aplicaciones clínicas de SGLT-2 se sigan ampliando, la farmacovigilancia en curso, los ensayos clínicos inclusivos y los estudios comparativos de seguridad serán esenciales para perfeccionar aún más su perfil beneficio-riesgo y optimizar su uso seguro en diversas poblaciones de pacientes.

abstract_en: To review available evidence in the management of established bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). We conducted a structured, domain-specific narrative review of PubMed (MEDLINE) from 2000 to 2025, including randomized trials, cohort studies, systematic reviews, and clinical guidelines in preterm infants with established BPD, with qualitative synthesis across predefined management domains. Published studies support oxygen saturation targets of 90-95% for most infants, with slightly higher targets used for those with pulmonary hypertension. Chronic-phase ventilation strategies accommodating heterogeneous lung mechanics are associated with improved synchrony and gas exchange. Diuretics provide only a transient benefit and are associated with growth and electrolyte disturbances. Systemic corticosteroids may facilitate extubation in selected infants, while inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators lack evidence for routine use. Chronic management of established BPD is supported by limited data. Current evidence for infants after 36 weeks' PMA favors careful oxygen titration, chronic-phase ventilation strategies, and selective pharmacologic therapy.

abstract_en: To evaluate the effectiveness of home-based exercise (HBE) interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) in cancer survivors. A comprehensive search of seven electronic databases was conducted for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 2000 to October 2025. The participants were cancer survivors who had received cardiotoxic therapies. The interventions were structured HBE programmes. Eligible studies were those that reported on any outcomes related to CTR-CVT. The primary outcomes included direct cardiotoxicity parameters (e.g., left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] and global longitudinal strain [GLS]) and cardiac biomarkers (e.g., troponins and B-type natriuretic peptide); clinical cardiovascular events (e.g., heart failure and arrhythmias); cardiorespiratory fitness (e.g., peak oxygen uptake [VO2 peak]); and (d) functional capacity (e.g., the six-minute walk test [6MWT]). Two researchers independently performed the study selection, data extraction, and methodological quality assessment. Meta-analyses were conducted using R software. Ten RCTs involving 851 participants were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that the HBE interventions significantly improved VO2 peak (MD = 2.35 mL/kg/min, 95% CI: 1.26 to 3.43, p < 0.001), which indicated improved cardiorespiratory fitness. Subgroup analysis found larger effects for longer-duration interventions (24 to 52 weeks), mHealth use, and cancer Stage III/IV. Evidence on direct cardiotoxicity parameters and biomarkers was limited, as only one study assessed these outcomes. No significant improvements were found in the 6MWT or health-related quality of life (HRQoL). While HBE improved cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 peak) and mitigated functional decline in cancer survivors, its ability to prevent CTR-CVT was unproven. Future adequately powered trials should incorporate direct cardiotoxicity assessments to establish true cardioprotective efficacy and implementation studies to optimise real-world delivery. not applicable.

Para evaluar la efectividad de las intervenciones de ejercicio en el hogar (HBE) sobre la aptitud cardiorrespiratoria y la toxicidad cardiovascular relacionada con el tratamiento del cáncer (CTR-CVT) en sobrevivientes de cáncer. Se realizó una búsqueda exhaustiva de siete bases de datos electrónicas para ensayos controlados aleatorios (RCT) publicados entre enero de 2000 y octubre de 2025. Los participantes fueron sobrevivientes de cáncer que habían recibido terapias cardiotóxicas. Las intervenciones fueron programas estructurados de HBE. Los estudios elegibles fueron aquellos que reportaron sobre cualquier resultado relacionado con CTR-CVT. Los resultados primarios incluyeron parámetros de cardiotoxicidad directa (por ejemplo, fracción de eyección del ventrículo izquierdo [FEVI] y cepa longitudinal global [SGL]) y biomarcadores cardíacos (por ejemplo, troponinas y péptido natriurético del tipo B); eventos cardiovasculares clínicos (por ejemplo, insuficiencia cardíaca y arritmias); aptitud cardiorrespiratoria (por ejemplo, pico de absorción de oxígeno [VO2 pico]); y d) capacidad funcional (por ejemplo, la prueba a pie de seis minutos [6MWT]). Dos investigadores realizaron independientemente la selección del estudio, extracción de datos y evaluación de la calidad metodológica. El metaanálisis demostró que las intervenciones del HBE mejoraron significativamente el pico de VO2 (MD = 2,35 mL/kg/min, IC 95%: 1,26 a 3,43, p < 0,001), lo que indicó una mejor aptitud cardiorrespiratoria.El análisis del subgrupo encontró efectos mayores para intervenciones de mayor duración (24 a 52 semanas), uso de mHealth y cáncer Estadio III/IV. La evidencia sobre parámetros de cardiotoxicidad directa y biomarcadores fue limitada, ya que solo un estudio evaluó estos resultados.No se encontraron mejoras significativas en el 6MWT o calidad de vida relacionada con la salud (HRQoL).Mientras que el HBE mejoró la aptitud cardiorrespiratoria (pico VO2) y mitiplicó el deterioro funcional en sobrevivientes de cáncer, su capacidad para prevenir CTR-CVT no fue probada. Los futuros ensayos con una potencia adecuada deben incorporar evaluaciones directas de cardiotoxicidad para establecer una verdadera eficacia cardioprotectora y estudios de implementación para optimizar la entrega en el mundo real.

abstract_en:
Introduction
Dyslipidaemia remains a major contributor to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and many patients fail to achieve recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets despite statin therapy or are unable to tolerate statins. Oral non-statin therapies have emerged as important alternatives; however, their comparative efficacy and safety remain unclear.Methods
We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central up to December 2025 for clinical trials evaluating these medications in adults with dyslipidaemia. Primary outcomes were percent and absolute changes in LDL-C, while secondary outcomes included other lipid parameters and safety profile. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed.Results
Forty-three trials comprising 17,021 participants were included. Combination therapies showed the greatest efficacy, with obicetrapib 10 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg achieving the largest reduction in percent LDL-C (-49.15%; 95% CI: -59.42 to -38.89), followed by bempedoic acid plus ezetimibe (-36.90%; 95% CI: -44.65 to -29.15). Obicetrapib also showed substantial improvements in HDL-C and ApoB. Safety outcomes were generally reassuring, with no significant increase in serious adverse events, myalgia, headache, or elevated liver enzymes; however, treatment discontinuation was higher with bempedoic acid 180 mg and colesevelam 3.75 g. The certainty of evidence was low to very low for many efficacy outcomes, primarily because of heterogeneity and imprecision.Conclusions
Oral non-statin combination therapies, particularly obicetrapib plus ezetimibe and bempedoic acid plus ezetimibe, provide the most effective LDL-C lowering and are valuable for patients with statin intolerance or residual risk. Ezetimibe remains a well-tolerated option. Long-term cardiovascular outcome trials are needed to confirm clinical benefit.

abstract_en: The integration of anthracyclines with HER2-targeted agents in neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer has been limited by cardiotoxicity concerns. This randomized phase II METIS trial (NCT04172259) assessed whether concurrent pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD)-containing chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab/pertuzumab) could improve efficacy without increasing cardiac risk. A total of 156 patients with stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer were randomized to a PLD-based concurrent regimen or an epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (EC)-based sequential regimen. The PLD-based concurrent group achieved a higher pathological complete response (pCR) rate (67.5% vs. 48.7%; difference, 18.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.6-34.0; P = 0.033) compared with the EC-based sequential group, with greater benefit in hormone receptor-positive disease (58.7% vs. 36.7%) and stage II tumors (82.1% vs. 48.0%). After a median follow-up of 37.5 months, fewer event-free survival (EFS) events occurred in the PLD-based concurrent group (3 vs. 8), yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.35 (95% CI, 0.09-1.32; P = 0.105). The estimated 3-year EFS rates were 96.0% (95% CI, 88.1-98.7) versus 90.7% (95% CI, 81.5-95.6). Achieving pCR was significantly associated with improved EFS (HR = 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.71; P = 0.006). Cardiac safety was comparable, with no symptomatic cardiac dysfunction and only one grade ≥3 cardiotoxicity in the EC-based sequential group. These findings support PLD-based concurrent therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as an effective and safe neoadjuvant option for high-risk HER2-positive breast cancer, warranting further evaluation in phase III trials.

abstract_en:
Background
An unmet need persists for optimal myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia. We investigated whether decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide (DAC-BuCy) conditioning reduced the risk of relapse compared with busulfan-cyclophosphamide (BuCy) conditioning.Methods
In this open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at eight transplantation centres in China, eligible patients were aged 14-65 years, had morphologically confirmed KMT2A-rearranged leukaemia, and had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) before HSCT to DAC-BuCy (intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m2 once a day on days -14 to -10, intravenous busulfan 3·2 mg/kg once a day on days -7 to -4, and intravenous cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg once a day on days -3 to -2) or BuCy (same dose and duration of busulfan and cyclophosphamide). Randomisation was done with permuted blocks (block size four) with no stratification and was implemented through an independent, interactive, web-based response system. The primary endpoint was 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse in the intention-to-treat population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03596892) and is complete.Findings
Between May 1, 2019, and Jan 31, 2023, 130 patients were randomised to receive a DAC-BuCy (n=65; 34 [52%] female and 31 [48%] male) or BuCy (n=65; 29 [45%] female and 36 [55%] male) regimen. Median follow-up was 34·7 months (IQR 30·2-52·5). 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 12% (95% CI 6-22) in the DAC-BuCy group and 29% (19-41) in the BuCy group (hazard ratio 0·41 [0·20-0·87]; p=0·017). The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were infections or infestations (DAC-BuCy group 27 [42%] and BuCy group 25 [38%]), acute graft-versus-host disease (DAC-BuCy group 23 [35%] and BuCy group 22 [34%]), and gastrointestinal disorders (DAC-BuCy group 14 [22%] and BuCy group 15 [23%]). Four (6%) patients in the DAC-BuCy group and five (8%) patients in the BuCy group died from adverse events, of which two were due to regimen-related toxicities: one nervous system disorder in the DAC-BuCy group and one cardiac disorder in the BuCy group.Interpretation
The addition of decitabine to BuCy conditioning reduced the risk of relapse with an acceptable safety profile in adult patients with KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia and could be a suitable therapeutic option for this population.Funding

abstract_en: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults. ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed). Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group). In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists. Los criterios de valoración de la eficacia fueron evaluados principalmente por el régimen de tratamiento y en todos los participantes asignados al azar. La seguridad fue evaluada en los participantes que recibieron al menos una dosis de tratamiento en el estudio. abstract_en: The timing of anticoagulation resumption in patients who experience ischemic stroke despite ongoing anticoagulation and develop haemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains uncertain. We aimed to describe the characteristics and outcomes of patients with HT after a breakthrough ischemic stroke and to explore the association between anticoagulation resumption timing and the model-predicted balance of recurrent ischemic and bleeding risks in this high-risk population. We analysed data from patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke receiving anticoagulation therapy from the multicentre ASPERA-R registry. Analyses focused on patients with HT. HT was defined according to the Heidelberg Bleeding Classification based on brain imaging within 24 hours and categorized as haemorrhagic infarction (HI) or parenchymal hematoma (PH). Anticoagulation resumption and its timing were determined by treating clinicians and were not randomized. Landmark Cox regression models were used to evaluate recurrent ischemic events and moderate-to-severe bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Restricted cubic spline models and exploratory net clinical benefit analyses integrating ischemic and bleeding risks were used to assess the relationship between anticoagulation resumption timing and model-predicted combined risk, overall and across clinically relevant subgroups. Among 1,555 patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, 269 (17.3%) developed HT, of whom 170 (63.2%) resumed anticoagulation and contributed to the restart-timing analyses. At 90 days, patients with HT had higher crude rates of recurrent ischemic events (27.1% vs 13.8%), moderate-to-severe bleeding (7.4% vs 2.8%), and mortality (34.2% vs 17.7%) compared with patients without HT. In landmark analyses, HT was not associated with recurrent ischemic events (HR 1.42, 95% CI 0.85-2.37) but remained strongly associated with moderate-to-severe bleeding (HR 3.39, 95% CI 1.61-7.13). Exploratory net clinical benefit analyses showed that the model-predicted combined risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke in the overall HT population, with substantial uncertainty around this estimate. HT is a marker of poor prognosis in patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, with an increased risk of bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Among selected patients who resumed anticoagulation, exploratory modelling suggested that the combined predicted ischemic and bleeding risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke. Given the non-randomized treatment timing and potential for treatment-selection bias, this estimate is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

El tiempo de reanudación de la anticoagulación en pacientes con ictus isquémico a pesar de la anticoagulación en curso y de la transformación hemorrágica (TC) sigue siendo incierto, con el objetivo de describir las características y los resultados de los pacientes con ictus isquémico tras un ictus isquémico disgresivo y explorar la asociación entre el tiempo de reanudación de la anticoagulación y el equilibrio predicho por el modelo de riesgos isquémicos recurrentes y hemorrágicos en esta población de alto riesgo, analizando los datos de los pacientes con ictus isquémico disgresivo que recibieron terapia anticoagulación del registro multicéntrico ASPERA-R. La HT se definió de acuerdo con la Clasificación Heidelberg de Sangrado basada en imágenes cerebrales dentro de las 24 horas y categorizada como infarto hemorrágico (HI) o hematoma parenquimatoso (PH). La reanudación de la anticoagulación y su cronometría fueron determinadas por los médicos y no fueron aleatorias. Para evaluar la relación entre el tiempo de reanudación de la anticoagulación y el riesgo combinado predicho por el modelo, en general y en subgrupos clínicamente relevantes, se utilizaron modelos de splines cúbicos restringidos y análisis de beneficios clínicos netos exploratorios que integraban riesgos isquémicos y hemorrágicos; entre 1.555 pacientes con ictus isquémico irruptivo, 269 (17,3%) desarrollaron TC, de los cuales 170 (63,2%) reanudaron la anticoagulación y contribuyeron a los análisis de tiempos de reanudación; a los 90 días, los pacientes con TC presentaron tasas brutas más altas de eventos isquémicos recurrentes (27,1% frente a 13,8%), hemorragia moderada a grave (7,4% frente a 2,8%) y mortalidad (34,2% frente a 17,7%) en comparación con los pacientes sin TC. En los análisis de puntos de referencia, la HT no se asoció con eventos isquémicos recurrentes (CRI 1,42, IC 95% 0,85-2,37), pero se mantuvo fuertemente asociada con hemorragias moderadas a graves (CRI 3,39, IC 95% 1,61-7,13). Los análisis exploratorios de beneficio clínico neto mostraron que el riesgo combinado predicho por el modelo alcanzó su nadir aproximadamente 10 días después del accidente cerebrovascular en la población total de TC, con incertidumbre sustancial alrededor de esta estimación. Entre los pacientes seleccionados que reanudaron la anticoagulación, la modelización exploratoria sugiere que el riesgo isquémico y hemorrágico combinado alcanzó su nadir aproximadamente 10 días después del accidente cerebrovascular. Dada la cronología no aleatoria del tratamiento y el potencial de sesgo de selección del tratamiento, esta estimación es generadora de hipótesis y requiere validación prospectiva.

abstract_en: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States and disproportionately affects racial/ethnic minoritized populations, low-income communities, older adults, and rural residents. Behavioral interventions can reduce cardiovascular risk, yet traditional programs face scalability barriers, including high costs and limited reach. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the efficacy and equity of patient-directed AI tools that support health education and behavior change for cardiovascular health. Using PRISMA-ScR elements, we searched 10 databases (January 2010 to December 2025), yielding 19 empirical studies evaluating Generation 2.0 AI systems aligned with the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework. Of these, five were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and 14 were nonrandomized (quasi-experimental, observational, or early-stage) studies. AI-enabled interventions such as conversational agents, machine-learning models, and reinforcement-learning systems addressed hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, and related conditions. Among the RCTs, one demonstrated superiority of an AI-powered program over usual care (AI-delivered Diabetes Prevention Program), whereas the remaining four reported outcomes equivalent or non-inferior to standard behavioral care. Effects were most apparent in high-intensity interventions that paired machine learning-based personalization with structured behavioral curricula, although the multi-component nature of these programs limits inference about AI-specific contributions. Across nonrandomized studies, greater engagement intensity was consistently associated with improved cardiometabolic outcomes, although causal attribution to AI-specific mechanisms remains limited. Most studies had small samples, short follow-up, and limited reporting on safety and equity. Technology-intensive interventions were concentrated in higher-resourced settings, and populations with limited health literacy showed reduced engagement. Overall, evidence supports cautious optimism that AI can meaningfully scale personalized cardiovascular prevention; however, realizing that equitable and clinically meaningful impact will require rigorous trials with longer follow-up, explicit behavioral science integration, safety-conscious governance, and equity-centered strategies addressing digital determinants of health.

Las enfermedades cardiovasculares (CVD) son la principal causa de muerte en los Estados Unidos y afectan desproporcionadamente a las poblaciones minorizadas raciales/étnicas, comunidades de bajos ingresos, adultos mayores y residentes rurales. Las intervenciones conductuales pueden reducir el riesgo cardiovascular, pero los programas tradicionales enfrentan barreras de escalabilidad, incluyendo altos costos y alcance limitado. Esta revisión narrativa sintetiza evidencia sobre la eficacia y equidad de las herramientas de IA dirigidas por los pacientes que apoyan la educación en salud y el cambio de comportamiento para la salud cardiovascular. Utilizando los elementos PRISMA-ScR, buscamos 10 bases de datos (enero 2010 a diciembre 2025), produciendo 19 estudios empíricos que evaluaban sistemas de IA de la generación 2.0 alineados con el marco esencial 8 (LE8) de la American Heart Association. De éstos, cinco fueron ensayos controlados aleatorios (RCTs), y 14 fueron estudios no aleatorizados (cuasi experimentales, observacionales o en etapas tempranas). Intervenciones habilitadas para la IA como agentes conversacionales, modelos de aprendizaje automático y sistemas de aprendizaje de refuerzos abordaron hipertensión, diabetes, insuficiencia cardíaca y condiciones relacionadas. Entre los ECA, uno demostró superioridad de un programa impulsado por IA sobre la atención habitual (Programa de Prevención de Diabetes dado por IA), mientras que los otros cuatro reportaron resultados equivalentes o no inferiores a la atención estándar de comportamiento.Los efectos fueron más evidentes en intervenciones de alta intensidad que combinaron la personalización basada en aprendizaje automático con currículos de comportamiento estructurados, aunque la naturaleza multicomponente de estos programas limita la inferencia sobre las contribuciones específicas de IA. En estudios no aleatorizados, una mayor intensidad de compromiso se asoció consistentemente con mejores resultados cardiometabólicos, aunque la atribución causal a mecanismos específicos de IA sigue siendo limitada. La mayoría de los estudios tenían muestras pequeñas, un seguimiento corto y una información limitada sobre seguridad y equidad. Las intervenciones intensivas en tecnología se concentraron en entornos con mayores recursos, y las poblaciones con una limitada alfabetización en salud mostraron un menor compromiso. En general, la evidencia apoya un optimismo cauteloso de que la IA puede escalar significativamente la prevención cardiovascular personalizada; sin embargo, darse cuenta de que un impacto equitativo y clínicamente significativo requerirá ensayos rigurosos con un seguimiento más prolongado, una integración explícita de la ciencia del comportamiento, una gobernanza consciente de la seguridad y estrategias centradas en la equidad que abordan los determinantes digitales de la salud.

title: Decoding Stroke-Heart Syndrome: A Translational Framework Linking Cerebral Injury to Cardiovascular Dysfunction.
